sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, The Right Color is a simple yet challenging game that requires you to match the name of a color with its corresponding visual representation. The game features a wide range of colors, from basic red, blue, and green to more complex shades and hues. As you play through the levels, the game gets progressively harder, introducing new colors and more complex patterns to identify.

One of the most interesting aspects of The Right Color is its ability to tap into the Stroop effect, a psychological phenomenon in which the brain has difficulty identifying the color of a word when the word itself is a different color. This effect is evident in the game's design, as the colors and words are carefully chosen to trigger this response. By leveraging the Stroop effect, The Right Color creates a sense of tension and challenge that keeps players engaged and motivated.

The game's core mechanics are easy to learn but difficult to master. As you progress through the levels, you'll need to develop strategies and techniques to improve your accuracy and speed.
